t: A sharifian dynasty from the Draa valley that ruled Morocco from Marrakesh and Fez between 1510 and 1659.
It won the Battle of Alcácer Quibir in 1578, where three kings died, and kept Morocco outside the Ottoman Empire.
Ahmad al-Mansur grew rich on sugar and Saharan gold and conquered Songhai, but his death in 1603 opened a ruinous civil war.
dyk: In 1612 the library of Sultan Zidan, sent by ship to safety during the civil war, was seized by Spanish vessels and ended up in the Escorial, where much of it remains.
ev: The tribes of the Sus proclaim Muhammad al-Qa’im leader of the holy war against Portugal
Muhammad al-Shaykh takes Agadir from the Portuguese
The Saadis take Fez from the Wattasids
Victory over Sebastian of Portugal at the Battle of Alcácer Quibir
Judar Pasha defeats Songhai at the Battle of Tondibi
Death of Ahmad al-Mansur and start of civil war among his sons
Morisco corsairs found the Republic of Salé
The last Saadi sultan is killed in Marrakesh
